text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No generative AI or personal data review recorded","detail":"The proposal uses an LLM (generative AI) on drivers' GPS location history, which is personal data, to draft disciplinary warnings that affect drivers. The only review noted is 'Ops leadership supports the pilot', which is not a legal, privacy, or AI governance review.","evidence_quote":"Ops leadership supports the pilot.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record privacy/legal review of GPS data use and generative AI review/approval, plus HR/labor review of the warning process, before launch."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No guardrails for warning quality, fairness, or driver impact","detail":"The proposal changes how drivers are disciplined but has only an earnings guardrail. It lacks guardrails such as driver attrition/retention, warning accuracy or manager override/edit rate, dispute/appeal rate, and fairness across driver groups.","evidence_quote":"- Driver Hourly Earnings: must not fall below baseline.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as driver attrition, warning dispute/appeal rate, manager rejection/edit rate of drafts, and delivery completion rate, and monitor for disparate impact."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration is under 14 days of standard and mismatched to the metric","detail":"The plan has a 4-week experiment, but the success target is set 'within 12 weeks', so the test ends well before the target can be observed. Randomizing by market with few units also raises power concerns, and no number of markets or cluster-adjusted power is given.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by market. Duration: 4 weeks. MDE: 0.3 incidents per 10,000 trips, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align test duration with the 12-week measurement horizon, and state the number of markets and cluster-adjusted power calculations."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Time-study claim lacks a verifiable source and quantification","detail":"The claim that managers 'spend hours' drafting warnings is attributed only to a generic 'LMD ops time study' with no link, date, or figures, so the problem size cannot be verified.","evidence_quote":"Operations managers spend hours drafting warnings to drivers with repeated service issues (source: LMD ops time study).","citations":[],"recommendation":"Link the time study and cite the actual measured time per warning and volume."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric does not measure the problem or causal path","detail":"The stated problem is manager time spent drafting warnings, and the proposal addresses service issues, but the success metric is Driver Safety Incident Rate. This is not tied to the proposal's mechanism, and no metric measures time saved or service-issue reduction.","evidence_quote":"- Driver Safety Incident Rate: baseline 3.1 per 10,000 trips, target 2.6 within 12 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Define success metrics that match the problem, such as manager drafting time per warning and repeat service-issue rate, using canonical glossary definitions."}]}
